questions.q: What distinguishes a governed tag from an ordinary Unity Catalog tag?
options: A governed tag has a tag policy restricting its allowed values and who can assign it
A governed tag can only be applied to columns, never to tables
A governed tag is visible only to the user who created it
A governed tag automatically deletes the data it's attached to after 90 days
questions.explain: Governed tags add a tag policy: administrators define allowed values and control which users/groups can assign the tag, enforced consistently across the account.

questions.q: In the Catalog Explorer tag-assignment dialog, how are system tags (like system.certification_status) visually distinguished from user-created governed tags?
options: A wrench icon, versus a lock icon for user-created governed tags
They appear in red text
They are listed in a completely separate dialog
They have no visual distinction at all
questions.explain: Governed tags are marked with a lock icon; system governed tags (Databricks-defined, not editable) carry a wrench icon instead.

questions.q: At which level of the Unity Catalog object hierarchy do tags NOT automatically inherit from their parent?
options: Columns
Schemas
Tables
Catalogs
questions.explain: Tags applied to a catalog or schema flow down to everything inside, except at the column level, which never inherits and must always be tagged directly.

questions.q: In `CREATE POLICY mask_pii_for_hr ON CATALOG catalog_a COLUMN MASK mask_pii TO \`account users\` EXCEPT \`HR admins\` FOR TABLES WHEN has_tag('HR') MATCH COLUMNS has_tag('PII') AS pii_col ON COLUMN pii_col;`, what determines which columns get masked?
options: Any column tagged 'PII' on any table in catalog_a that is itself tagged 'HR'
Every column in catalog_a, regardless of tags
Only columns named 'pii_col' literally
Only columns in tables owned by the HR admins group
questions.explain: The WHEN clause scopes to tables tagged 'HR'; MATCH COLUMNS has_tag('PII') picks out the columns tagged 'PII' within those tables — the policy applies dynamically to any object matching both conditions.

questions.q: What is the main practical advantage of an ABAC policy over writing a separate column mask for each table?
options: One policy automatically covers every matching table and column, including ones created after the policy was written
ABAC policies run faster than table-level column masks
ABAC policies don't require any SQL functions
ABAC policies can only be written by the table owner
questions.explain: Because ABAC policies match by tag rather than by object name, they apply automatically to new objects as they're created and tagged, without writing a new policy for each one.
